title: Kerberos service ticket presented with no matching upstream TGT issuance
event_type: Windows Security channel, Event ID 4769 (A Kerberos service ticket was requested), correlated against an absent Event ID 4768 for the same logon session

fields.label: Corresponding 4768 for TargetLogonId 0x3F2A9C1
fields.value: None found in the same session window

callouts.explanation: A legitimately issued ticket always has an issuance event (4768) upstream of a later use event (4769) in the same logon session; the absence of that matching 4768 — not any single field value on the 4769 itself — is the tell that this ticket may be forged rather than issued by the KDC.

The session identifier used to correlate ticket issuance against ticket use across the 4768/4769 pair; a stateful correlation engine keys on this field, not on username or source IP, since both are reused across unrelated sessions.

AES256 encryption on this ticket does not indicate legitimacy — a forged Golden or Silver Ticket can carry any encryption type the forger chooses, so this field alone cannot distinguish a valid ticket from a forged one.

The host presenting this service ticket; on its own this looks like an ordinary client-to-service request, which is exactly why the issuance/use mismatch, not this field, carries the detection signal.

note: Conceptual and illustrative only, constructed to show the issuance/use correlation gap described in the surrounding text — not a captured screenshot from a real Kerberos exchange or any product interface.
